title: Cost optimization automation: batching & caching defaults, quantization profiles, unit-economics tooling
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: reduce unit inference cost by providing safe, automated defaults and tooling for batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles. This PR implements a coordinated set of changes across the serving runtime, the Optimize recommendation engine, the Redwood Console, and docs/examples to make cost-saving defaults opt-in-by-default for new deployments and to expose unit-economics metrics for operators.

What this PR does (high level):
- Serving runtime: introduces a new DefaultBatchPolicy that tunes target batch sizes and latency SLO-aware windowing per-model family; enables safe prefix/KV caching defaults for recurrent chat workloads with configurable cache TTLs and eviction heuristics.
- Quantization profiles: adds curated quantization profile recipes (q4_0/q4_1/q8_0) for common model families, a profile registry, and an automated validation job that runs downstream quality checks against a small eval prompt set.
- Redwood Optimize and Console: adds an automated recommendations API that suggests batching and quantization pairs, shows estimated per-token unit cost impact and expected latency delta, and a UI panel with a "Simulate savings" flow.
- Unit economics: adds a per-route unit-cost estimator that combines runtime telemetry (tokens, GPU time) with pricing configs to compute Estimated Cost Per 1M tokens and projected monthly savings when applying recommendations.
- Tests & safety: adds e2e smoke tests, quantization regression tests, and performance bench harness scripts; defaults are gated behind a feature flag (optimize.cost_automation.enable) for gradual rollout.

Implementation notes:
- Runtime changes: abstracted batch policy interface to allow dynamic selection; cache enabled via config and safe by default (only caches prefix and non-sensitive routes, logged decisions). KV cache improvements include more aggressive aggregation on short-sequence chat patterns which increases batching efficiency without impacting tail latency for single-turn requests.
- Quant profiles: profiles are stored as YAML recipes under runtime/quant_profiles/, validated at CI and loaded via profile registry with backward-compatible fallback to the model's previous execution path. Validation job compares logits on a small corpus and asserts no regressions above a defined threshold.
- Optimize API: new endpoint POST /v1/optimize/recommendations takes a usage sample and returns ranked recommendation objects with estimated savings. The UI surfaces a one-click apply flow for Dedicated/Private customers; for hosted customers it surfaces a simulation and a rollout plan suggestion.

Checklist:
- [x] Add DefaultBatchPolicy and cache default config
- [x] Add quantization profile registry and CI validation
- [x] Add Optimize API and Console UI panel (frontend + backend)
- [x] Add unit-economics estimator and telemetry integration
- [x] Add tests (unit, regression, e2e smoke)
- [x] Add docs and migration notes

Backwards compatibility & rollout: changes are feature-flag controlled. Existing customers see no change unless they opt-in. Quantization profiles require an explicit apply step; the runtime will not auto-apply lossy quantization to pinned model versions.

Related Linear: ENG-4821 (batching defaults) and ENG-4850 (quant profiles + unit economics).
